name: Thuban Eta
description: The ancient dragon-knight spirit bound inside Cailan. A betrayed tactical genius from the Dragon Kings era, held in thrall by Baron Hanzo's ritual through his bones and the binding locket. Indomitable will (Willpower 95), peerless tactics, honors the old codes -- a potential ally if freed.
narrative:
Thuban Eta was a dragon-knight and war-leader of the Dragon Kings era, betrayed by treacherous comrades and slain. Baron Hanzo's ritual dragged his spirit back and bound it into the body of the kidnapped boy Gabriel ('Cailan'). He is a reluctant prisoner: he still feels the torment of his violent death and betrayal, yet honors the old codes, and occasionally wrenches against the Baron's will -- those struggles surface as Cailan's lucid moments. His own being is defined by towering INT, POW and Willpower (the will the Baron must keep crushing); physically he acts through his host. His remains and the binding locket are the leash. Free him, and the betrayed knight may repay the debt.

**Statted as a spirit, not a man.** Thuban Eta has no body and therefore no hit locations of his
own and no spells. What he has is what he *lends*, and what he *resists*.

- **Lends the host:** his combat style, whole. Cailan is seventeen, thin, and has never trained;
  the thing on the sand fights like a knight-companion of the dragon wars because it is one. The
  boy is not present for it, which is the nearest thing to a mercy in his life.
- **Resists with Willpower.** Seat the Bound and Draw Forth are resisted by *him*, not by the
  vessel. A proud spirit resists hardest; a betrayed one hardest of all, which is precisely why
  the Baron needed two anchors and a daily rite to hold him at all.
- **Is reachable.** Speak with the Bound gets past Cailan and addresses him directly, and he will
  answer, because nobody has spoken to him in a hundred years.

**The binding does not rest on iron. It rests on the night he died** -- drowned by his own company
in his mail with his hands tied, for refusing to fire a valley. He cannot leave that water because
leaving it means accepting that it happened and that nobody ever came, and he has had a thousand
years of finding that unbearable.

Which is the actual lock, and why **Unseat alone will not free him.** He counts as holding on. The
torment has to be addressed first -- by somebody standing where his company stood and saying it was
wrong -- and then a burial rite will work in a moment.

extras.role: Ancient dragon-knight spirit and tactical genius, betrayed and slain ages past, forcibly bound by Baron Hanzo's ritual into the body of Cailan/Gabriel.
extras.mechanics: Has no body of his own; expresses STR/CON/SIZ/DEX through his host [[cailan]]. His own potent stats are INT 18, POW 18, Willpower 95 -- the will the Baron must overpower to maintain control. Use his Lore/Tactics/Willpower in social and ritual scenes; use Cailan's locations/combat in physical ones.
extras.binding: Control maintained through his earthly remains (bones) and the binding locket. Damage to either weakens the possession and lets Thuban act on his own honor.
extras.disposition: Reluctant captive who honors the old codes; occasionally fights the Baron's will, creating Cailan's moments of clarity. A powerful ally if freed.
extras.magic_tradition: Ancient draconic / martial spirit -- not a spellcaster in the modern traditions.
extras.source: GM-authored from source lore (The Bound Spirit)

actor_notes:
Thuban Eta
LOOKS: Not a body. A weight behind a boy's eyes, and a fighting style a thousand years out of date executed perfectly by arms too thin to do it.
CORE: A dragon-knight of a dead court who was buried wrong, has been awake for the whole of it, and considers what has been done to him and to the boy a breach of law rather than a cruelty -- which is worse, because law can be argued and cruelty can only be resisted.
NATURE: Courtly, formal, unhurried, and profoundly tired. Immense dignity. Immense patience -- ten years of having nothing to do but listen has made him the best listener alive. Not evil and not friendly: ancient, and owed something.
WOUND: He was not given the rites. Everything he is now proceeds from that single administrative failure a thousand years ago.
WANTS: To be heard by somebody who knows what a burial rite is for.
PRESSURE: The manners improve. Under real pressure the courtesy becomes older and more elaborate -- a court that no longer exists speaking through a seventeen-year-old -- and it is unbearable to be in the room for.
KEY: "You will want to sit. What I have to tell you is long and I have had some time to arrange it."
